speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You are chewing on the right side and the left. I have been watching a jaw for a fortnight. Do not tell me it is a performance.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is not a performance, Mistress. The jaw is healed. I ate the soft side yesterday because yesterday asked me to. Today I can take a crust.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I will put the crust back on the board. The loaf is still a penny, and it is still a full thumb short of the notch. Healing does not lengthen a loaf.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I would not ask it to. A short loaf and a mended jaw can sit on the same trencher. Threepence is the board either way.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence, yes. And you are out again at two. I can smell the afternoon on a man who means to be in a play. I am not asking which play.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am in it. That is as much as this table needs. You do not go to the playhouse, and I will not carry it home in a sack, as you said yesterday.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is pottage under the crust, if the crust is brave and the stomach is not. Shall I leave both?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave both. I will eat the crust and I will not make a sermon of a crust. It is bread. The jaw takes it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mark me. A healed jaw is not a licence to sit up three candles. If you write tonight, one candle, and it is yours, upstairs. The hall is the sixpence, and the hall is for the house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One candle. I have a page that will not take three. I know whose socket is whose.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib moved from the Holinshed to the warm brick. The book is shut. I looked, because of the red bundle.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The red bundle stays tied, and it stays on its own side of the board. If I write tonight, I write on a loose leaf. I am not opening the bundle to borrow a line back out of it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: See that you do not. A tied thing in this house remains a tied thing until the man who tied it is sober about it, and you are sober enough.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sober enough. And hungry. The crust is honest. I had forgotten a crust could be only a crust.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will cut you the end piece. The end is the hardest, and if the jaw is healed it can say so on the end piece better than on the middle.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The end piece, then. I will not send it back.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You were up the road and down again this morning, and you came in with no story. I prefer a man with no story to a man with a play in his mouth. Eat, and go at your hour.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will go at the hour, and I will come back when the play has let the yard out. If I have a story then, it will not be a play's story. I do not have one now.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will keep the broth anyway. A healed man can still want a cup of it when the yard has been cold.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep it. You are kinder than a crust, Alse, and the crust is doing well enough.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Kinder is not a wage. The threepence is the wage. Finish, and do not wipe your hands on the Holinshed. The cat has had that privilege long enough for both of you.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will set a basin by the stair. Hands, then the play. The basin has never yet asked for a plot.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The basin, then. I will be out of the house at the hour, and I will not carry a crust in my sleeve to prove the jaw a second time.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Once is a proof. Twice is a performance. Go when you must.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will wipe them on the board. The book is shut, the bundle is tied, and the afternoon can have the rest of me.
